theory_units.caution: Unless players' positions and looks are duplicated when the camera is moved, a jump cut will result.

theory_units.title: Duplicating Player Position/Looks for Dialogue Continuity
theory_units.summary: Players' positions and looks must be duplicated when the camera is moved during dialogue scenes to prevent jump cuts.
theory_units.applies_when: Whenever the camera angle changes within a dialogue scene.
theory_units.expected_effect: Preserves continuous eyelines and spatial relationships between characters, which are critical for audience comprehension and immersion in dialogue scenes.
theory_units.caution: Failure to duplicate will result in a jump cut.

theory_units.title: Precision for Cutting on Action in Dialogue Scenes
theory_units.summary: Cutting on action in dialogue scenes (e.g., player sitting into close-up) requires precise duplication of dialogue and movement, as performed in the wider shot.
theory_units.applies_when: When attempting match-on-action cuts in dialogue scenes.
theory_units.expected_effect: Achieves a seamless blend of action and dialogue across cuts, maintaining the natural flow of the performance.

theory_units.title: Rehearsal Emphasis for Dialogue Scene Continuity
theory_units.summary: Dialogue scenes should be carefully rehearsed with emphasis on what a player does, and where he stands or moves as he speaks his lines, rather than just what he says.
theory_units.applies_when: During rehearsals for any scene containing dialogue.
theory_units.expected_effect: Ensures actors' physical performances are consistent and repeatable, providing the editor with match-cutting opportunities for both action and dialogue.
theory_units.caution: If both action and dialogue do not match precisely, the film editor will have difficulties in match-cutting the sequence.

theory_units.title: Master Scene Technique & Precision Matching
theory_units.summary: If the master scene technique is used, players must repeat their actions and dialogue precisely in closer shots to avoid action mis-matches that force cuts to reaction shots or cut-aways.
theory_units.applies_when: When using the master scene approach, where a scene is first filmed in a wide master shot, then covered with closer shots.
theory_units.expected_effect: Enables seamless match-cutting between the master and closer shots, preserving the continuous flow of dialogue and action.
theory_units.caution: Action mis-matches may force the editor to cut to reaction shots of the listening actor, or resort to cut-away reaction close-ups of other players.

theory_units.title: Overlap for Triple-Take Match-Cutting
theory_units.summary: If the triple-take technique is used and the sequence is filmed shot-for-shot, both action and dialogue should be overlapped to ensure match-cutting.
theory_units.applies_when: When filming individual shots in a shot-for-shot manner, rather than a continuous performance.
theory_units.expected_effect: Provides the editor with sufficient material to precisely align both the visual and auditory elements, ensuring a perfect match cut.

theory_units.title: Sound Flow Across Scenes
theory_units.summary: Sound should flow across scenes, rather than beginning and ending with the picture in each individual shot, for maximum effectiveness.
theory_units.applies_when: When editing any scene involving dialogue or continuous ambient sound.
theory_units.expected_effect: Creates a smoother, more immersive auditory experience, avoiding abrupt edits that would disrupt the flow of dialogue and audience engagement.
theory_units.caution: Avoids abrupt editing that would result if the player's image and his speech start and stop simultaneously.

theory_units.title: Camera Duration on Speaker
theory_units.summary: The camera should rarely remain on the speaker for the duration of his speech, unless what he says is more important than the reaction of listening players.
theory_units.applies_when: When filming or editing dialogue scenes involving multiple characters.
theory_units.expected_effect: Maintains audience engagement by showing the emotional impact of dialogue on listeners, adding depth and dynamism to the scene.

theory_units.title: Providing Editor with Comprehensive Coverage
theory_units.summary: The editor should have players' speeches as well as reaction shots of all concerned, so that he may edit the sequence as he sees fit.
theory_units.applies_when: During filming of dialogue scenes.
theory_units.expected_effect: Gives the editor maximum creative control and problem-solving ability to construct the most effective dialogue sequence.

theory_units.title: Silent Reaction Shots for Dialogue Manipulation
theory_units.summary: Silent reaction shots allow considerable editorial cheating if dialogue must be removed or additional 'wild' (unsynchronized) lines inserted later, without resulting in a jump-cut.
theory_units.applies_when: When there's a need to modify dialogue in post-production, especially to shorten or extend speeches.
theory_units.expected_effect: Facilitates seamless dialogue adjustments by providing visual cover, as the audience is watching reactions rather than the speaking actor.

theory_units.title: Filming Full Over-the-Shoulder for Dialogue Reactions
theory_units.summary: Over-the-shoulder close-ups, where two players talk back and forth, should be filmed in their entirety on each player, providing reaction shots of both as they actually listen.
theory_units.applies_when: When filming two-person dialogue scenes, especially with OTS coverage.
theory_units.expected_effect: Provides matched reaction shots to thoughts expressed, resulting in better interplay between actors because the actual dialogue is heard over the actor's reaction.
theory_units.caution: May appear wasteful of film; saving film by shooting all-purpose silent reactions may harm actor's performance and restrict editor.

theory_units.title: Continuous Sound Recording During Dialogue
theory_units.summary: The camera should never be stopped in the middle of important dialogue; the entire speech should be recorded, even if the picture is not required at that point, for editorial flexibility.
theory_units.applies_when: During sound recording on set for dialogue scenes.
theory_units.expected_effect: Provides the editor with complete audio takes, allowing them to extend dialogue over reaction shots or other scenes, even if the original visual wasn't intended to be used.

theory_units.title: Predetermining Cuts by Sound Track Content
theory_units.summary: All camera cuts should be predetermined by the sound track content and marked in the script.
theory_units.applies_when: During script breakdown and pre-production planning for sound-synced scenes.
theory_units.expected_effect: Ensures a tightly integrated visual and audio narrative, simplifying editing by pre-planning cut points based on dialogue or sound cues.

theory_units.title: Avoiding Jump-Cuts in Long Speeches with Reaction Shots
theory_units.summary: Jump-cuts may be avoided whenever portions of a long speech are presented (e.g., highlights), by cutting to reaction shots of the listening audience.
theory_units.applies_when: When editing lengthy speeches where only highlights are needed, or portions must be removed.
theory_units.expected_effect: Allows shortening of speeches or removal of segments without the viewer being aware, maintaining seamless visual flow and focus on the impact of the speech.

theory_units.title: Using Dissolves for Speaker Continuity During Speech Cuts
theory_units.summary: If the camera must remain on the speaker and avoid jump-cuts caused by removal of portions of the speech, dissolves should be used each time a cut is made to smooth the change in the speaker's appearance or position.
theory_units.applies_when: When editing a long speech where the camera must stay on the speaker, and segments need to be removed.
theory_units.expected_effect: Smooths visual changes in the speaker's appearance or position that would otherwise result in jarring jump-cuts when parts of their speech are edited out.

theory_units.title: Technical Uniformity in Film Production
theory_units.summary: Technical elements of a film (photographic treatment, lighting, color, exposure, sound, etc.) should be uniform in production quality to avoid noticeable visual or audio differences.
theory_units.applies_when: Throughout all stages of production, from principal photography to final delivery.
theory_units.expected_effect: Maintains audience immersion by eliminating distracting technical discrepancies and upholding professional production standards.
theory_units.caution: A mis-match or distracting change, unless deliberately inserted for a special effect, may disturb the audience. Poorly recorded sound, perceptible changes in lighting, unbalanced color are unacceptable.

theory_units.title: Documentary Photographic Style
theory_units.summary: Documentary subjects should be represented realistically and not overly styled for visual beauty, while still striving for aesthetic quality within the confines of realism.
theory_units.applies_when: Filming documentary subjects, engineering, military, educational, business, industrial, or in-plant films.
theory_units.expected_effect: Authenticity and audience connection to the real subject, while maintaining professional visual appeal.
theory_units.caution: Avoid a dull, unimaginative, or mechanical style; beauty and realism can be combined, but the primary aim is to 'sell' the subject, not the photography.

theory_units.title: Technical Uniformity for Immersion
theory_units.summary: Maintain uniform production quality across all visual (lighting, color, exposure) and audio elements in a professional film to prevent technical discrepancies from distracting the audience and breaking the storytelling spell.
theory_units.applies_when: During production and post-production of any professional film.
theory_units.expected_effect: Seamless audience immersion and sustained storytelling, free from distracting technical flaws.
theory_units.caution: Technical discrepancies are distracting and break the storytelling spell, as editors cannot correct many visual or audio imperfections beyond basic salvage.

theory_units.title: Purposeful Shot
theory_units.summary: Every individual shot should contribute meaningfully to the narrative, making a clear point and building interest as the film progresses.
theory_units.applies_when: Planning and executing individual shots within any narrative film, especially for non-theatrical cameraman/directors.
theory_units.expected_effect: Maintains audience interest and ensures coherent narrative progression.
theory_units.caution: Technically perfect or excellently-composed shots have little meaning if presented illogically or incoherently.

theory_units.title: Directing Audience Attention to Key Elements
theory_units.summary: Anticipate what the audience will be most interested in and actively guide their attention by moving in for close-ups of important actions, objects, or significant simultaneous events.
theory_units.applies_when: During production, when choosing what to frame and how to move the camera within a scene.
theory_units.expected_effect: Captures and holds audience attention, ensures the audience cares about the depicted elements, and enhances narrative clarity.
theory_units.caution: None.

theory_units.title: Event Breakdown and Shot Planning
theory_units.summary: Deconstruct an event into individual shots by first deciding the required shot type for each portion, then considering the optimal camera angle and movement, and planning for the insertion of cut-in and cut-away close-ups.
theory_units.applies_when: During pre-production or 'off-the-cuff' filming, to ensure comprehensive and effective coverage for a story-telling motion picture.
theory_units.expected_effect: Footage that can be easily assembled into a coherent story, heightened audience interest, and the best portrayal of action.
theory_units.caution: None.

theory_units.title: Providing Reaction Shots
theory_units.summary: Anticipate and film reaction shots to effectively serve storytelling or editorial purposes, enriching the narrative and audience's emotional connection.
theory_units.applies_when: During production, especially when filming dialogue, emotionally charged events, or sequences where character response is key.
theory_units.expected_effect: Enhances narrative depth, provides crucial editorial options, and strengthens audience emotional response and understanding.
theory_units.caution: Editors cannot insert non-existent close-ups, so these must be filmed on set.

theory_units.title: Maximizing Editorial Choices During Production
theory_units.summary: Employ specific shooting techniques, such as overlapping actions between shots, filming clean entrances and exits, and introducing pauses in moving camera shots, to provide the editor with the greatest number of choices for assembly.
theory_units.applies_when: During all filming, especially when aiming for high editorial flexibility or shooting 'off-the-cuff'.
theory_units.expected_effect: An easier and more flexible editing process, the ability to solve potential problems in post-production, and a smoother final cut.
theory_units.caution: Poor filming techniques that result in scenes that 'do not cut' are inexcusable, as editors cannot work cinematic miracles.

theory_units.title: Maintaining Continuity of Player Position and Eye-line
theory_units.summary: Ensure players maintain correct positions, looks, and eye-lines between consecutive shots, as editors cannot fix these discrepancies, which lead to unmatched cuts and break immersion.
theory_units.applies_when: Filming any sequence where shots will be cut together, particularly dialogue or action sequences.
theory_units.expected_effect: Seamless transitions between shots, preventing audience confusion and maintaining narrative immersion.
theory_units.caution: Editors cannot change screen directions, players' looks, or match consecutive shots if players are out of position or looking the wrong way.

theory_units.title: Strategic Use of Close-ups for Impact
theory_units.summary: Close-ups are powerful storytelling devices that should be reserved for vital moments in the story to ensure their intended dramatic impact and visual clarity on the audience.
theory_units.applies_when: When planning to emphasize a specific narrative point, emotion, or detail within a scene.
theory_units.expected_effect: Heightened dramatic impact, visual clarity, and increased audience engagement.
theory_units.caution: Improperly used close-ups can confuse the audience and detract attention, neutralizing their cinematic effectiveness.

theory_units.title: Standard Close-up Designations for People
theory_units.summary: Understand and apply standard terminology for different close-up framings on people to ensure consistent visual storytelling and clear communication.
theory_units.applies_when: Composing close-ups of people or communicating shot intentions in scripts.
theory_units.expected_effect: Clarity in communication of shot intention and consistent visual language across a film.
theory_units.caution: A close-up of a person, unless specified, is generally regarded as a Head and Shoulder Close-Up.

theory_units.title: Extreme Close-ups for Magnification and Emphasis
theory_units.summary: Utilize extreme close-ups to greatly magnify tiny objects, small areas, or crucial portions of a subject, presenting them full-screen for ultra-dramatic significance and clarity.
theory_units.applies_when: When precise detail of small machine parts, calibrations, intricate actions, or specific facial features (e.g., ear, nose, lips, eyes) requires maximum emphasis.
theory_units.expected_effect: Ultra-dramatic significance, visual clarification of minute details, and intense audience focus on the specific element.
theory_units.caution: None.

theory_units.title: Over-the-Shoulder for POV Transition
theory_units.summary: Use over-the-shoulder close-ups as an effective transitional device to smoothly move the audience from an objective camera angle to a point-of-view (POV) close-up, enhancing immersion.
theory_units.applies_when: Transitioning from an objective shot to a POV shot, particularly in dialogue sequences or when a character's perspective is about to be emphasized.
theory_units.expected_effect: A smoother, less abrupt transition to a POV, improving audience immersion in the character's perspective.
theory_units.caution: While the OTS can be eliminated, the cut to a POV close-up becomes much smoother if preceded by an over-the-shoulder shot.

theory_units.title: Matching Over-the-Shoulder Shot Pairs
theory_units.summary: Film opposing over-the-shoulder close-ups for a pair of players in a similar manner, ensuring that camera distance, camera angle, and image size approximate each other to present a uniform appearance.
theory_units.applies_when: Filming dialogue exchanges or interactions between two characters using opposing over-the-shoulder shots.
theory_units.expected_effect: Visual uniformity and smooth cutting between the two perspectives, maintaining audience immersion and preventing visual jarring.
theory_units.caution: Exact matching is sometimes difficult due to differences in body contour, head size, and height of players; approximation is sufficient but crucial.

theory_units.title: Framing the Foreground Player in Over-the-Shoulder Shots
theory_units.summary: In an over-the-shoulder shot, angle and frame the foreground player from a rear three-quarter view, showing their back and side with only their cheek line visible (no nose extending past it), to clearly distinguish it from a two-shot.
theory_units.applies_when: Composing over-the-shoulder close-ups where a foreground player partially obstructs the view of another.
theory_units.expected_effect: Clear distinction between an OTS and a two-shot, maintaining focus on the background player, and preserving audience perspective.
theory_units.caution: If the nearer player's facial features (especially the nose past the cheek line) are visible, the scene becomes a two-shot, altering the intended dynamic.

theory_units.title: Objective Cut-in Close-up
theory_units.summary: An objective cut-in close-up captures a magnified portion of the main action from an unseen observer's viewpoint, bringing the viewer closer without involving them personally in the scene.
theory_units.applies_when: To bring the viewer closer to a significant player, object, or action within the main scene while maintaining an impersonal, observational perspective.
theory_units.expected_effect: Increased audience proximity to the subject, enhancing detail and focus, without breaking the fourth wall or adopting a character's direct view.
theory_units.caution: None.

theory_units.title: Subjective Cut-in Close-up
theory_units.summary: A subjective cut-in close-up is filmed with the player looking directly into the camera lens, creating direct engagement and communication with the audience.
theory_units.applies_when: Used rarely in dramatic theatrical films (for asides), but commonly in non-theatrical films (news, commercials, documentaries) where a commentator or expert needs to speak directly to the viewer.
theory_units.expected_effect: Direct audience involvement, a personal connection, and the feeling that the speaker is communicating directly with them.
theory_units.caution: Rarely employed in dramatic theatrical films as it breaks immersion; primarily used for direct commentary or address.

theory_units.title: Over-the-Shoulder Cut-in Close-up
theory_units.summary: An over-the-shoulder cut-in close-up frames the main action or a player's reaction over the shoulder of an opposing player, typically filmed in matched pairs for dialogue exchanges.
theory_units.applies_when: Filming dialogue exchanges where two players confront each other, providing context of the other player's presence while focusing on the speaker.
theory_units.expected_effect: Contextualizes conversations by showing one character's perspective while keeping the other's presence felt; common and natural for dialogue.
theory_units.caution: Generally filmed in matched pairs to ensure smooth cutting between perspectives.

theory_units.title: Point-of-View (POV) Cut-in Close-up
theory_units.summary: A POV cut-in close-up is filmed from the viewpoint of a player in the scene, positioning the camera at the side of the player to show an opposing player, object, or small-scale action from their direct perspective.
theory_units.applies_when: To involve the audience most directly in the screen action by having them view the scene through a character's eyes.
theory_units.expected_effect: Stronger audience identification with the player and greater involvement in the event, creating a highly subjective experience.
theory_units.caution: The on-screen player's look must always be slightly to the side of the lens, not directly into it. If player heights vary, the look must be 'cheated' just above or below the lens accordingly.

theory_units.title: Establish Characters with Two-Shot Before OTS/POV Series
theory_units.summary: Before moving into a series of over-the-shoulder (OTS) or point-of-view (POV) close-ups, first identify the involved players with a two-shot to prevent audience confusion regarding character relationships and positioning.
theory_units.applies_when: Introducing a sequence of OTS or POV shots involving multiple characters, especially at the beginning of a conversation or interaction.
theory_units.expected_effect: Audience clarity on player identities, their spatial relationships, and smooth transitions into closer, more intimate perspectives.
theory_units.caution: Failure to establish characters beforehand can lead to audience confusion about 'who is talking to whom' or 'where everyone is'.

theory_units.title: Using Cut-ins for Narrative Highlights
theory_units.summary: Employ cut-in close-ups to magnify and emphasize narrative highlights such as important dialogue, player action, or reaction, drawing the viewer closer to the subject for dramatic impact.
theory_units.applies_when: When dramatic emphasis or increased audience attention is required for a specific detail, line of dialogue, or emotional moment.
theory_units.expected_effect: Heightened dramatic impact, concentrated audience attention on key information, and visual clarity of significant moments.
theory_units.caution: None.

theory_units.title: Using Cut-ins for Isolation and Focus
theory_units.summary: Employ cut-in close-ups to isolate significant subject matter, eliminating non-essential elements from view, thereby concentrating audience attention on an important action, object, or expression.
theory_units.applies_when: When needing to draw exclusive audience attention to a specific detail, action, or emotion by removing distractions.
theory_units.expected_effect: Concentrated audience attention, clear visibility of significant details, and effective removal of visual clutter.
theory_units.caution: None.

theory_units.title: Using Cut-ins to Magnify Small Actions
theory_units.summary: Utilize cut-in close-ups to visually clarify small-scale actions that would be difficult to discern without strain in wider shots, satisfying audience curiosity and preventing loss of interest.
theory_units.applies_when: When an action is too small to be clearly viewed in a medium or long shot, potentially causing viewer strain or disinterest (e.g., soldering, instrument dials).
theory_units.expected_effect: Visual clarity of intricate actions, satisfied audience curiosity, and sustained audience interest.
theory_units.caution: None.

theory_units.title: Using Cut-ins for Time Lapse and Compression
theory_units.summary: Insert cut-in close-ups to shorten the depicted time interval of lengthy, tedious, or repetitious actions, allowing for the removal of unessential footage while giving the impression of a complete event.
theory_units.applies_when: When needing to condense long or repetitive processes (e.g., manufacturing, typing, repairs) without losing the audience's understanding of the complete event.
theory_units.expected_effect: Efficient pacing, avoidance of audience tedium, and audience acceptance of condensed time through implied completeness.
theory_units.caution: None.

theory_units.title: Using Cut-ins to Mask Jump-Cuts
theory_units.summary: Insert a cut-in close-up between two shots that would otherwise create a jump-cut (due to mis-matched action, position, or looks) to distract the audience and allow the discrepancy to go unnoticed.
theory_units.applies_when: When needing to smooth over continuity errors or unmatchable shots that occur due to player position changes, looks, or movement between takes.
theory_units.expected_effect: Seamless transitions despite underlying continuity problems, preventing audience distraction from technical errors.
theory_units.caution: Implies a previous filming error; ideally, continuity should be maintained during shooting.

theory_units.title: Using Cut-ins for Hidden/Unfilmable Action
theory_units.summary: Utilize cut-in close-ups of related elements (e.g., control panels, operator reactions, external indicators) to represent or imply hidden actions that cannot be directly filmed due to physical constraints or danger.
theory_units.applies_when: When an action is physically concealed (e.g., inside a machine), inaccessible, or too dangerous to film directly, but needs to be conveyed to the audience.
theory_units.expected_effect: Clear communication of unfilmable processes, efficient storytelling, and avoidance of visual gaps by implying action through visible correlates.
theory_units.caution: None.

theory_units.title: Establishing Cut-in Close-ups with Wider Shots
theory_units.summary: Always establish a cut-in close-up with a preceding wider shot (long or medium long) to ensure the audience is aware of the close-up subject's location and context within the overall scene.
theory_units.applies_when: Before introducing a cut-in close-up of a player, object, or action, to prevent audience disorientation.
theory_units.expected_effect: Prevents audience confusion, properly orientates the viewer to spatial relationships, and maintains narrative continuity.
theory_units.caution: Failure to establish a close-up will confuse the audience; the close-up's significance may be lost if the audience is disoriented.

theory_units.title: Re-establishing Shots After Close-up Sequences
theory_units.summary: After a sequence of closer shots, especially if there's significant player or camera movement, provide a re-establishing shot to re-orient the audience to the overall scene and current player positions.
theory_units.applies_when: Following a series of tight close-ups where player movement or camera movement might have caused audience disorientation.
theory_units.expected_effect: Prevents audience confusion about spatial relationships, maintains narrative continuity, and allows the audience to comprehend the significance of closer shots in context.
theory_units.caution: Audience may lose track of player whereabouts, breaking narrative continuity; if too little of the set is seen, an un-re-established cut can mystify the audience.

theory_units.title: Opening with an Unestablished Close-up (for Effect)
theory_units.summary: On rare occasions, a close-up can open a sequence without a preceding establishing shot, particularly to create suspense or confusion, provided its context is eventually revealed or it match-cuts smoothly.
theory_units.applies_when: When intentionally creating suspense, bewilderment, or dramatic intrigue, or when the close-up's context is immediately resolved by a pull-back or subsequent match-cut.
theory_units.expected_effect: Creates immediate intrigue, suspense, or dramatic focus; can temporarily disorient the audience for narrative purposes.
theory_units.caution: Requires careful handling; must eventually match-cut with the following shot or be revealed as a portion of the overall action when the camera pulls back, to avoid permanent confusion.

theory_units.title: Cut-away Close-up Definition and Principle
theory_units.summary: A cut-away close-up depicts secondary action happening simultaneously elsewhere, distinct from the main scene but always narratively connected, directly or indirectly.
theory_units.applies_when: When introducing parallel action, reaction, or commentary that is separate from but related to the main ongoing scene.
theory_units.expected_effect: Expands narrative scope, provides context, or offers commentary on the primary event.
theory_units.caution: Cut-aways must always be narratively connected to the main story, even if separated spatially.

theory_units.title: Objective Cut-away Close-up
theory_units.summary: An objective cut-away close-up captures a secondary subject from an impersonal viewpoint, bringing the viewer closer to a related event without personal involvement.
theory_units.applies_when: To show a related, secondary action or subject from a neutral, unseen observer's perspective, for exposition or context.
theory_units.expected_effect: Increased audience proximity to the subject while maintaining an impersonal viewing experience of a related event.
theory_units.caution: None.

theory_units.title: Subjective Cut-away Close-up
theory_units.summary: A subjective cut-away close-up features a person looking directly into the camera lens, engaging the audience personally, typically used in non-theatrical explanatory films.
theory_units.applies_when: Used in news reels, documentary reports, or similar explanatory films to create a strong personal connection, making the viewer feel directly addressed (e.g., an engineer explaining a rig).
theory_units.expected_effect: Stronger audience attention and personal involvement, making the communication more impactful and direct.
theory_units.caution: Rarely used in theatrical films as it breaks narrative immersion; more suitable for direct address formats.

theory_units.title: Point-of-View (POV) Cut-away Close-up
theory_units.summary: A POV cut-away close-up shows a secondary subject or action from the viewpoint of a player in the main scene, increasing audience interest and identification with that player.
theory_units.applies_when: To increase audience interest and identification with a player by showing a related, secondary action or object (e.g., a clock, another player, a cocking gun) from their perspective.
theory_units.expected_effect: Stronger audience identity with the player and greater involvement in the event, by experiencing their perspective directly.
theory_units.caution: None.

theory_units.title: Using Cut-aways for Off-screen Player Reactions
theory_units.summary: Employ cut-away close-ups to depict the reactions of off-screen players, as their emotional response can often be more significant or interesting to the audience than the primary on-screen action or dialogue.
theory_units.applies_when: When an off-screen player's emotional response to dialogue or events is crucial to the narrative or holds more audience interest than the primary action.
theory_units.expected_effect: Shifts audience focus to emotional impact, deepens character understanding, and maintains engagement by highlighting emotional stakes.
theory_units.caution: None.

theory_units.title: Using Cut-aways to Cue Audience Reaction
theory_units.summary: Insert a cut-away reaction close-up of a player portraying a specific emotion (e.g., fear, tension, awe, pity) to stimulate a similar, receptive mood or feeling in the viewer.
theory_units.applies_when: To guide or elicit a specific emotional response from the audience to the preceding or ongoing main action.
theory_units.expected_effect: Creates a desired audience mood, facilitates emotional connection and empathy, and enhances the impact of the scene's emotional tone.
theory_units.caution: None.

theory_units.title: Using Cut-aways for Visual Commentary
theory_units.summary: Insert cut-away close-ups depicting related or symbolic actions (e.g., animals, 'man-in-the-street' reactions) to provide visual commentary, irony, or subtext on the principal event, dialogue, or narration.
theory_units.applies_when: When wanting to add a layer of meaning, irony, or social comment through visual parallels, contrasts, or symbolic imagery.
theory_units.expected_effect: Enriches narrative meaning, provides subtext, and enhances audience understanding or emotional response through association or juxtaposition.
theory_units.caution: None.

theory_units.title: Using Cut-Away Close-Ups for Distraction or Directional Coverage
theory_units.summary: Cut-away close-ups can be employed to distract the audience, cover a directional change in screen travel, or obscure editorial necessities like jump-cuts.
theory_units.applies_when: When needing to divert audience attention, mask an edit, or smooth a directional change within a sequence.
theory_units.expected_effect: Audience distraction or seamless transition, making editorial choices less apparent.
theory_units.caution: None explicitly stated here, but implies judicious use to avoid narrative disruption.

theory_units.title: Motivating Sequences with Cut-Away Close-Ups
theory_units.summary: Cut-away close-ups can effectively open a sequence by showing a motivating element that triggers the principal action or scene to follow.
theory_units.applies_when: When introducing a new sequence and desiring to quickly establish its driving force or context.
theory_units.expected_effect: Engages the audience by presenting a clear impetus for the upcoming action, creating a strong opening.

theory_units.title: Implying Gruesome or Expensive Events with Reaction Shots
theory_units.summary: To avoid depicting overly gruesome or prohibitively expensive scenes directly, use cut-away close-ups of bystander reactions, accompanied by sound effects, to convey the event's impact.
theory_units.applies_when: When the actual depiction of an event (e.g., war, accident, disaster) is too revolting for viewers or too costly to stage.
theory_units.expected_effect: Conveys the severity of an event while protecting audience sensibilities or managing production costs, allowing the audience to infer the details.

theory_units.title: Establishing Cut-Away Close-Ups
theory_units.summary: Generally, cut-away close-ups do not need prior establishment as they are not part of the main event; however, if a player was previously seen in a wider shot and moved off-screen, their reappearance in a cut-away requires careful matching of their 'look' (gaze direction) to avoid audience confusion.
theory_units.applies_when: When filming any cut-away close-up, especially those involving characters who have been previously established in wider shots.
theory_units.expected_effect: Maintains audience comprehension and continuity, preventing confusion about character positioning relative to the main action.
theory_units.caution: If an opposite look is filmed, the audience may be led to believe that the supporting player has crossed to the opposite side of the principal players. Because the look is wrong, the audience would be confused.

theory_units.title: Pre-Establishing Cut-Away Location ('Planting')
theory_units.summary: A cut-away close-up's location can be established earlier in a sequence by 'planting' it as part of an overall scene, allowing the audience to recall its presence later.
theory_units.applies_when: When planning to use a cut-away close-up of a player or object whose location might not be immediately obvious later in the sequence.
theory_units.expected_effect: Ensures the audience understands the context and location of the cut-away, preventing confusion when it appears later.

theory_units.title: Preference for Cut-In vs. Cut-Away Close-Ups
theory_units.summary: It is generally preferable to use a cut-in close-up over a cut-away to heighten audience interest, as cut-ins are more intimately involved with the principal action. Cut-aways should only be used for significant story points or editorial necessities.
theory_units.applies_when: When deciding between a cut-in and a cut-away close-up.
theory_units.expected_effect: Cut-ins create a more intimate and involved audience experience; cut-aways, if not justified, can disrupt the narrative.
theory_units.caution: Unless the cut-away close-up makes a significant story point, it should not be employed. Otherwise, it may disrupt the narrative. An exception would be the insertion of a cut-away close-up intended to distract the audience, in order to cover a jump-cut or some other editorial necessity.

theory_units.title: Choosing Point-of-View for Close-Ups
theory_units.summary: For close-ups, a player's point-of-view (POV) camera angle is usually best, as it provides the audience with a more intimate view of the subject.
theory_units.applies_when: When selecting the camera angle for a close-up, particularly if audience empathy or intimate connection is desired.
theory_units.expected_effect: Enhances audience intimacy and engagement by allowing them to see the subject from a character's perspective.

theory_units.title: Matching Looks in Cut-In Close-Ups
theory_units.summary: Cut-in close-ups must consistently match the 'looks' (direction of gaze) of players in surrounding scenes to preserve continuity along the action axis and prevent audience confusion.
theory_units.applies_when: When filming cut-in close-ups that are part of a continuous main action.
theory_units.expected_effect: Maintains seamless spatial and relational continuity, ensuring players appear to be looking at each other correctly.
theory_units.caution: If the look varies during the long or medium shots, the corresponding look must be filmed in the cut-in close-up used for that particular point in the sequence. A cut-in close-up filmed with the wrong look - right instead of left, or left instead of right - is editorially useless because the player will look away from, rather than toward, opposing player.

theory_units.title: Avoiding Direct Gaze into Lens
theory_units.summary: A player must never look directly into the camera lens when crossing the camera, as this breaks the fourth wall and can disrupt the narrative.
theory_units.applies_when: When a player's movement involves crossing the camera's field of view.
theory_units.expected_effect: Maintains the illusion of the narrative world and prevents breaking audience immersion.

theory_units.title: Positioning for Matched Point-of-View Looks
theory_units.summary: To ensure matched looks in opposing point-of-view close-ups, the off-screen player should be positioned as close as possible to the side of the camera, or a reference point should be provided, to ensure the on-screen player's head turn is appropriate.
theory_units.applies_when: When filming two-shots or sequences involving opposing point-of-view close-ups where players are meant to be looking at each other.
theory_units.expected_effect: Preserves the point-of-view relationship between players, making their interaction appear natural and consistent.
theory_units.caution: If the off-screen player stands too far from the side of the camera, the opposing on-screen player will have to turn his head - spoiling the point-of-view relationship of both players.

theory_units.title: Look Direction in Unrelated Cut-Away Close-Ups
theory_units.summary: Cut-away close-ups that are removed from the main event or intended to deliberately confuse the viewer may feature players looking in either direction. A series of unrelated cut-aways can be pictorially effective with alternate right and left looks.
theory_units.applies_when: When using cut-away close-ups for stylistic effect, to create intentional disorientation, or when they are not narratively tied to a specific location or interaction.
theory_units.expected_effect: Can enhance pictorial variety or contribute to an intentional feeling of disorientation or detachment.
theory_units.caution: This differs from cut-ins or narratively significant cut-aways, which require precise look matching.

theory_units.title: Look Direction for Telephone Conversations
theory_units.summary: When depicting players talking on the telephone, they should be filmed facing in opposite directions to create opposing looks, which infers they are relating to each other as if standing together.
theory_units.applies_when: When filming two or more players engaged in a telephone conversation.
theory_units.expected_effect: Conveys a sense of connection and dialogue between physically separated players, leveraging audience conditioning that opposing movements will meet and opposing looks infer relation.

theory_units.title: Editorial Attention for Cut-Away Close-Ups
theory_units.summary: Cut-away close-ups require as much editorial attention as cut-in close-ups, especially when the location of the player shown is narratively significant.
theory_units.applies_when: During the editing process for all types of close-ups.
theory_units.expected_effect: Ensures clarity and purpose in the use of cut-aways, contributing to overall narrative coherence.
theory_units.caution: Do not neglect cut-away close-ups under the assumption they are less important for matching than cut-in close-ups.

theory_units.title: Optimal Camera Angle for Close-Ups
theory_units.summary: A three-quarter to front-face camera angle is almost invariably best for close-ups, as it shows more facial facets and allows for good modeling of the face, even with flat front lighting if cross-lighted.
theory_units.applies_when: When framing a close-up, especially for actors, to maximize facial expression and dimensionality.
theory_units.expected_effect: Enhances the viewer's perception of facial features and emotions, providing a more engaging and aesthetically pleasing image.

theory_units.title: Caution with Profile Close-Ups
theory_units.summary: While profile close-ups offer pictorial variety, they require careful treatment to avoid a flat, 'cardboard cut-out' effect and lack the intimate eye-to-eye contact characteristic of three-quarter or POV angles.
theory_units.applies_when: When considering the use of a profile close-up.
theory_units.expected_effect: Provides visual diversity, but at the risk of reducing intimacy and creating a less dynamic image.
theory_units.caution: Require careful treatment to avoid a flat cardboard cut-out effect. The profile's single eye lacks the intimate eye-to-eye contact between player and audience characteristic of three-quarter angle, and particularly po-v.. close-ups.

theory_units.title: Avoiding 'Stolen' Telephoto Close-Ups in Staged Scenes
theory_units.summary: For staged sequences, avoid 'stealing' close-ups with long telephoto lenses from distant, long-shot camera positions. This practice results in poorly-angled, flat, and inadequately-lighted close-ups.
theory_units.applies_when: When filming staged sequences where dedicated close-up shots are required.
theory_units.expected_effect: Ensures high-quality, well-composed, and properly lit close-ups that are integral to the scene's emotional and visual impact.
theory_units.caution: Usually results in poorly-angled, flat, inadequately-lighted close-ups. While tolerable for uncontrollable action (e.g., newsreels), it is inexcusable on staged sequences.

theory_units.title: Dedicated Set-ups for Objective and POV Close-Ups
theory_units.summary: For staged sequences, the camera should be physically moved in and around to shoot objective or point-of-view close-ups of each player, rather than using the same camera set-up as a preceding wider shot.
theory_units.applies_when: When transitioning from a wider shot (e.g., a two-shot) to individual close-ups of players.
theory_units.expected_effect: Allows for optimal camera angles, lighting, and composition for each close-up, enhancing intimacy and visual quality.
theory_units.caution: Filming a pair of profile close-ups from the same camera set-up as a preceding two-shot generally results in close-ups which lack intimacy because players' features are flattened.

theory_units.title: Camera Height for Objective Close-Ups
theory_units.summary: Objective close-ups should generally be filmed from eye-level, but the camera height can be adjusted slightly higher or lower to match the overall camera treatment of the sequence or to solve particular facial problems.
theory_units.applies_when: When determining the camera height for an objective close-up.
theory_units.expected_effect: Maintains visual consistency within a sequence and can be subtly adapted to enhance a subject's appearance or match the established tone.

theory_units.title: Camera Height for Subjective Close-Ups
theory_units.summary: Subjective close-ups are best filmed from the eye-level of the person photographed, ensuring the subject is eye-to-eye with the camera lens and thus the audience. Higher or lower angles distort expression and create an awkward relationship.
theory_units.applies_when: When filming a subjective close-up where the camera represents the unseen viewer's eye.
theory_units.expected_effect: Establishes a direct, intimate eye-to-eye relationship between the subject and the audience, fostering connection.
theory_units.caution: If the camera is higher or lower, the subject must look up or down to look into the lens. The resulting expression on the subject is distorted, and may discourage the viewer from relating with him. A higher or lower than eye-level camera height places the audience above or below the subject, creating an awkward relationship.

theory_units.title: Camera Height for Point-of-View Close-Ups
theory_units.summary: Point-of-view (POV) close-ups should be filmed with the camera positioned at the eye-level of the opposing player whose viewpoint is being depicted. This presents the view as seen by the player involved.
theory_units.applies_when: When filming a close-up from a character's point-of-view, looking at another character, object, or event.
theory_units.expected_effect: Accurately represents the character's visual perspective, immersing the audience in their viewpoint.

theory_units.title: Cheating Camera Height in Point-of-View Shots
theory_units.summary: Considerable cheating of camera height is permissible in point-of-view shots. The camera can be positioned higher or lower to simulate differences in height (e.g., adult looking down at a child) or to exaggerate for psychological effect.
theory_units.applies_when: When a POV shot needs to convey a specific height relationship or psychological imbalance between subjects.
theory_units.expected_effect: Realistically or dramatically conveys height differences and can manipulate audience perception (e.g., making an adult appear taller to a child).
theory_units.caution: The camera position need not be at the exact height of the person involved.

theory_units.title: Camera Height for Over-the-Shoulder Close-Ups
theory_units.summary: Over-the-shoulder close-ups should be filmed as close as possible to the eye-level of the featured player, adjusting for foreground framing and proper modeling based on the height of the player in the foreground.
theory_units.applies_when: When filming an over-the-shoulder close-up, especially with players of differing heights.
theory_units.expected_effect: Achieves the best foreground framing, proper modeling of the featured player, and a natural perspective in the interaction.
theory_units.caution: Differences in height may sometimes be cheated by having a shorter player stand on a block, or a tall woman remove her high heel shoes.

theory_units.title: Consistency in Series of Close-Ups
theory_units.summary: A series of close-ups should maintain corresponding image sizes and, preferably, similar camera angles to ensure uniform screen appearance. Back-and-forth close-ups of opposing players should also be matched in image size and angle.
theory_units.applies_when: When planning or filming a sequence involving multiple close-ups.
theory_units.expected_effect: Creates a coherent and visually harmonious sequence, avoiding a 'hodge-podge' of shots that can disrupt viewer experience.
theory_units.caution: If different types of close-ups, or different angles, are mixed, a hodge-podge of shots will result.

theory_units.title: Varying Close-Up Series for Narrative Purpose
theory_units.summary: Unless narratively justified, close-ups should not be presented in a monotonous series merely to maintain uniformity. Each player should be filmed with the same change in image size and from the same angle to provide matched pairs for editing.
theory_units.applies_when: When designing a sequence featuring multiple close-ups of different players or objects.
theory_units.expected_effect: Ensures close-ups contribute to the story rather than just filling screen time, while still offering editorial flexibility.
theory_units.caution: Do not present close-ups in a monotonous series merely to maintain uniformity of size and angle unless for narrative reasons.

theory_units.title: Consistency in Repetitious Cut-Away Close-Ups
theory_units.summary: A series of repetitious cut-away close-ups of unrelated players or objects should maintain the same image size and similar or opposing camera angles/looks, offering options like alternating right and left looks or counterpoint angled tilts.
theory_units.applies_when: When compiling a series of independent cut-away close-ups (e.g., 'man-in-the-street' interviews, various objects).
theory_units.expected_effect: Achieves a coherent visual rhythm or creates specific pictorial effects, even with unrelated subjects.

theory_units.title: Logging Close-Up Technical Data
theory_units.summary: It is advisable to meticulously record technical data for close-ups, including lens focal length, camera angle (especially Dutch-tilt direction), and distances, to ensure uniformity and facilitate retakes, particularly when there are long intervals between filming matched shots.
theory_units.applies_when: During the filming of any close-up, particularly if it needs to be matched later or if retakes are anticipated.
theory_units.expected_effect: Ensures precise duplication of shots and maintains visual uniformity of close-ups throughout a production.
theory_units.caution: Do not trust to memory, especially if a long interval occurs between the filming of matched close-ups.

theory_units.title: Controlling Head Movement in Static Close-Ups
theory_units.summary: In tight, static close-ups, a player's head should not bob around, requiring continuous camera movement. Controllable subjects should be instructed to hold position. For uncontrollable subjects, use a shorter focal length lens to cover a wider area, allowing for a static camera.
theory_units.applies_when: When filming static close-ups, especially with restless or uncontrollable subjects.
theory_units.expected_effect: Maintains stable framing and avoids distracting camera adjustments, leading to a more professional and visually appealing shot.
theory_units.caution: Allows filming with a static camera, rather than constantly panning/tilting to follow a bobbing head, which is often seen in newsreels with telephoto lenses.

theory_units.title: Duplicating Player Movement for Cutting on Action
theory_units.summary: Player movement into and out of close-ups should be duplicated in both the wider shot and the close-up, providing the film editor with choices for cutting 'on the move' or 'on the action,' which results in a more fluid film.
theory_units.applies_when: When a player moves from a wider shot into a close-up, or vice-versa.
theory_units.expected_effect: Enables seamless transitions between shots, masking splices and creating a continuous flow of movement, avoiding a 'stop-and-go' appearance.
theory_units.caution: If the player is positioned in the frame for the close-up, rather than moved into position, the editor has no choice. He must move the player into position in the wider shot, and then cut to the already-positioned player in the close-up, which can severely handicap the editor.

theory_units.title: Technique for Moving into a Tight Head Close-Up
theory_units.summary: To facilitate a player moving into precise position for a static head close-up, the standing player can keep their feet static, bend their upper body to the side, and then swing their body back into a vertical position, perfectly framing the head.
theory_units.applies_when: When a player needs to move into a tight, static head close-up from a standing position.
theory_units.expected_effect: Allows for precise framing of the head in a tight close-up without requiring extensive camera adjustments.

theory_units.title: Filming Movement Out of Close-Ups
theory_units.summary: Movement out of a close-up is relatively simple to film and should always be captured if the player is to be 'picked up' on the move in the subsequent shot, to avoid limiting editorial choices.
theory_units.applies_when: Whenever a player exits a close-up and their movement is editorially useful in a following wider shot.
theory_units.expected_effect: Provides the editor with greater flexibility to shorten sequences gracefully and maintain fluid action across cuts.
theory_units.caution: Should the player not be moved out of the close-up, he must remain in his close-up position for next shot; and then be moved, during following medium or long shot, in order to continue action. The absence of moves into and out of close-ups may severely handicap the editor.

theory_units.title: Matching Tempo for Magnified Close-Up Movements
theory_units.summary: The timing of player movements in close-ups must match that in surrounding scenes, especially if movement flows across a cut. Small actions that appear greatly magnified on screen (e.g., throwing a switch) should be performed with deliberate slowness in the close-up to avoid appearing highly accelerated.
theory_units.applies_when: When filming close-ups of small, detailed actions that will be intercut with wider shots.
theory_units.expected_effect: Ensures smooth cutting on action and prevents magnified movements from appearing unnaturally fast or jarring on screen.
theory_units.caution: Differently-timed movements in wider shots and close-ups prevent cutting on action, and force the editor to resort to statically-positioned close-ups, after movement into the frame is completed.

theory_units.title: Efficient & Consistent Close-Up Set-Ups
theory_units.summary: For theatrical films, similar close-ups are often filmed at the same time to avoid duplicating camera set-ups. For technical films requiring continuity, marking camera positions, logging lens data, and diagramming lighting is essential to precisely duplicate shots over time.
theory_units.applies_when: When planning the filming schedule and set-up logistics for close-ups, especially in productions with complex continuity or limited time.
theory_units.expected_effect: Saves time and resources while ensuring technical matching of wider shots and close-ups, regardless of intervals between filming.

theory_units.title: Close-Up Background Selection
theory_units.summary: Close-ups should avoid 'busy' backgrounds with detailed designs, shiny surfaces, or distracting objects, unless narratively justified. Favor nondescript, softly-contrasting backgrounds, using receding pastel hues (cool blues, neutral grays) and avoiding primary or 'hot' advancing colors.
theory_units.applies_when: When composing any close-up shot.
theory_units.expected_effect: Ensures the audience's attention remains on the subject of the close-up, without competition from the background.
theory_units.caution: Possible exceptions include amusement parks (for gaiety) or TV commercials (for multi-facet reflections). In dramatic pictures, even a lamp with an ornate shade can be a provoking influence.

theory_units.title: Using Shallow Depth of Field for Close-Up Backgrounds
theory_units.summary: Throwing the background slightly out of focus is an effective technique for close-ups, but it should be avoided if lights, shiny objects, or highly reflective surfaces in the blurred background still distract the viewer, especially in color filming.
theory_units.applies_when: When using shallow depth of field for close-ups.
theory_units.expected_effect: Separates the subject from the background, enhancing focus on the main subject.
theory_units.caution: Avoid if lights, shiny objects, or highly reflective surfaces distract the viewer's attention from the players. This can be particularly disturbing in color filming, if shiny colored objects - such as tinted light bulbs - show up in the background.

theory_units.title: Avoiding Awkward Background Elements in Close-Ups
theory_units.summary: Plan camera angles for sequences to prevent background objects (lamps, trees, furniture, etc.) from awkwardly appearing behind players' heads in close-ups. Adjust camera angle, player position, or reposition props to avoid such distractions.
theory_units.applies_when: During scene blocking and camera setup, especially when integrating close-ups into a sequence.
theory_units.expected_effect: Maintains a clean and professional image, preventing visual clutter that draws attention away from the player.
theory_units.caution: If only a small portion of the offending object shows, it may be best to remove it completely, ensuring it is returned for subsequent wider shots if needed.

theory_units.title: Backgrounds for Documentary Close-Ups
theory_units.summary: For unscripted documentary or newsreel close-ups, take particular care to avoid backgrounds that might perplex or tease the audience with unfamiliar partial signs, insignias, or distracting wild designs. Neutral grays, pastel tints, or plain material are most suitable.
theory_units.applies_when: When filming close-ups in situations without introductory long or medium shots, such as interviews.
theory_units.expected_effect: Ensures the viewer's attention remains on the subject, avoiding confusion or distraction from ambiguous background elements.
theory_units.caution: In trying to solve what is missing, the viewer may pay less attention to the subject.

theory_units.title: Close-Up as Dramatic Sequence Opener (Mystery/Reveal)
theory_units.summary: A close-up can dramatically open a sequence to startle, confuse, or withhold information from the audience, revealing the full context only when the camera pulls back to a wider shot.
theory_units.applies_when: When introducing a new sequence with an intention to create immediate intrigue, shock, or to control the flow of information.
theory_units.expected_effect: Startles, confuses, or shocks the audience into paying attention, building suspense or delivering a surprise when the full context is disclosed.

theory_units.title: Object Close-Up as Motivational/Locale Opener
theory_units.summary: A sequence can open with a close-up of an object to motivate subsequent action, create suspense (e.g., ringing phone, gun), or establish the locale quickly (e.g., drink poured = bar).
theory_units.applies_when: When introducing a sequence and desiring to establish context, drive the plot, or create a specific mood through a symbolic or functional object.
theory_units.expected_effect: Motivates action, creates suspense, or efficiently establishes the setting, enhancing the narrative's immediate impact.

theory_units.title: Close-Ups as Transitional Devices
theory_units.summary: Pairs of close-ups, similar in size, motion, or content, serve as excellent bridging devices, blended optically or straight cut, to provide pictorial transitions between sequences or cover time/space shifts.
theory_units.applies_when: When transitioning between different sequences, locations, or points in time.
theory_units.expected_effect: Creates smooth and meaningful transitions, tying together disparate parts of the narrative visually.

theory_units.title: Using Sound with Close-Up Transitions
theory_units.summary: Sound can significantly enhance close-up transitions, using elements like repeated dialogue, questions and answers, or specific sound effects to tie together different players or settings across a cut.
theory_units.applies_when: When creating transitions between close-ups, especially if linking different characters or locations.
theory_units.expected_effect: Strengthens the connection between transitioning scenes, providing an additional layer of narrative coherence and emotional impact.

theory_units.title: Camera Movement for Close-Up Transitions
theory_units.summary: Camera movement (e.g., tilt, pan, dolly) can be effectively employed to move into and pull back from transitional close-up pairs, linking sequences with fluid motion.
theory_units.applies_when: When designing transitions between sequences that involve close-ups.
theory_units.expected_effect: Creates a dynamic and fluid transition, guiding the audience's eye and smoothly connecting the narrative elements.

theory_units.title: Purpose of Good Composition
theory_units.summary: Good composition involves arranging pictorial elements to form a unified, harmonious whole, planning player placement and movement to elicit favorable audience reactions and concentrating viewer attention on the most significant story elements.
theory_units.applies_when: During any stage of filmmaking that involves visual arrangement and staging.
theory_units.expected_effect: Motivates desired audience reactions and ensures clear communication of dramatic emphasis, making the story live in the viewer's mind.
theory_units.caution: The camera mechanically records all properly exposed, sharply focused images with equal clarity; the cameraman must direct dramatic emphasis non-mechanically.

theory_units.title: Flexibility of Compositional Rules
theory_units.summary: Compositional principles are pliable; dramatically striking scenes often result from deliberately breaking rules. However, one must thoroughly comprehend the rules and understand the 'why' behind breaking them to do so effectively.
theory_units.applies_when: When approaching composition, balancing traditional guidelines with creative expression.
theory_units.expected_effect: Allows for innovative and impactful visual storytelling that can transcend conventional beauty, if executed thoughtfully.
theory_units.caution: To break the rules effectively, it is first necessary to comprehend the rules thoroughly, and to realize why they are being broken.

theory_units.title: Deliberately Poor Composition for Effect
theory_units.summary: Intentionally employing unbalanced, cluttered, or poorly composed scenes can aid storytelling by irritating the audience and expressing a specific thematic need, such as the need for change or depicting distress.
theory_units.applies_when: When the narrative intention is to evoke irritation, discomfort, or to visually reinforce a problematic situation or theme (e.g., slum clearance).
theory_units.expected_effect: Irritates the audience, expresses a need for correction (e.g., decent housing), and creates a powerful pictorial and psychological impact that makes the audience subconsciously want to 'straighten' the scenes.

theory_units.title: Motion Picture Composition: Space and Time
theory_units.summary: Unlike still photography, motion picture composition exists in both space and time, involving a progression of varied-size images where space and time relationships constantly change due to player or camera movement.
theory_units.applies_when: When conceptualizing composition for moving images.
theory_units.expected_effect: Creates a dynamic and evolving visual experience, demanding consideration of how elements interact across both spatial and temporal axes.
theory_units.caution: This constantly-changing image pattern tends to complicate motion picture composition.

theory_units.title: Significance of Movement in Motion Picture Composition
theory_units.summary: Movement is the greatest asset of motion pictures, but if abused (e.g., using sheer movement to compensate for poor composition), it becomes a liability. Successful scenes result from thoughtful compositions combined with significant player and/or camera movements.
theory_units.applies_when: When incorporating movement of players or the camera into a scene.
theory_units.expected_effect: Enhances storytelling and audience engagement when movement is purposeful and thoughtfully composed; otherwise, it distracts and detracts.
theory_units.caution: If abused, however, movement - which should be the motion picture's greatest asset - can very easily become its greatest liability. Unsatisfactory scenes are the results of thoughtless compositions and meaningless player or camera movements, which distract rather than aid in the story-telling.

theory_units.title: Controlling Distracting Movement
theory_units.summary: The cameraman must guard against insignificant movement of subordinate players or unimportant objects within a scene, as the viewer's eye is easily attracted and distracted by any moving object, especially in quiet or static scenes.
theory_units.applies_when: During any scene, but particularly in quiet scenes that are more or less static in nature.
theory_units.expected_effect: Maintains audience focus on the principal player, action, or object by eliminating visual competition.

theory_units.title: Static Composition in Motion Pictures
theory_units.summary: Rules of static composition (for still photographs) can be successfully applied to motion picture scenes that have fixed pictorial elements.
theory_units.applies_when: When a motion picture scene consists of static or fixed pictorial elements.
theory_units.expected_effect: Aesthetically pleasing and balanced composition, similar to still photography.
theory_units.caution: None explicit, but implicitly, these rules may not apply to dynamic scenes.

theory_units.title: Dominance by Movement or Sound
theory_units.summary: Even if a scene breaks all compositional rules, the viewer's eye can still be attracted to a significant player or object if it is dominated by movement or sound.
theory_units.applies_when: When the primary goal is to direct viewer attention, potentially overriding traditional compositional aesthetics.
theory_units.expected_effect: Audience attention drawn to the intended focal point, regardless of visual composition.
theory_units.caution: This does not imply that good composition should be disregarded entirely.

theory_units.title: Conveying Awe and Grandeur
theory_units.summary: To convey a mood of awe, vastness, or grandeur of setting, use long shots or extreme long shots.
theory_units.applies_when: When the script requires the audience to feel awe or appreciate the vastness/grandeur of a setting.
theory_units.expected_effect: An emotional response of awe and a sense of large scale in the audience.

theory_units.title: Applying Good Composition in Static/Key Moments
theory_units.summary: Rules of good composition should be utilized whenever possible, especially for static action like establishing long shots, players at rest during dialogue, or whenever dramatic emphasis needs to be attracted to dominant subject matter.
theory_units.applies_when: In scenes with static elements, establishing shots, or when directing attention to a key subject.
theory_units.expected_effect: Clear focus, aesthetic pleasure, and effective communication of dramatic emphasis.
theory_units.caution: Aesthetic values should not be neglected due to eye-and-ear attractions of movement and sound.

theory_units.title: Continuous Composing
theory_units.summary: Players and objects should be harmoniously arranged and moved with artistic effect, requiring continuous composition as the scene progresses, regardless of player or camera movement.
theory_units.applies_when: Throughout any motion picture scene, especially those involving movement of subjects or camera.
theory_units.expected_effect: Consistently pleasing and effective visual composition, adapting to dynamic changes.

theory_units.title: Forms in Depth
theory_units.summary: Whenever possible, scenes should be composed in depth to impart a three-dimensional quality, as forms described in depth are compositionally stronger than those appearing flat on the screen surface.
theory_units.applies_when: Whenever the scene allows for arranging elements to create a sense of depth.
theory_units.expected_effect: A stronger, more engaging composition with a sense of realism and space.

theory_units.title: Line Placement: Avoiding Equal Division
theory_units.summary: For most effective composition, real lines (vertical, horizontal, or diagonal) should not divide the picture into equal parts, nor should strong vertical or horizontal lines be centered.
theory_units.applies_when: When composing a shot with prominent lines, such as horizons, poles, or natural boundaries.
theory_units.expected_effect: A more dynamic and visually interesting composition, preventing static or amateurish framing.
theory_units.caution: Avoid placing elements like telegraph poles or the horizon in the middle of the frame.

theory_units.title: Line Placement: Avoiding Parallelism
theory_units.summary: Straight lines should not parallel any side of the frame unless they form part of a repetitious pattern created by elements like buildings, columns, or trees.
theory_units.applies_when: When composing a shot with prominent straight lines.
theory_units.expected_effect: Avoids a static or boxy appearance, making the composition more dynamic, unless intentional for a pattern.
theory_units.caution: A single strong line at the side, top, or bottom should be irregular rather than perfectly vertical or horizontal.

theory_units.title: Line Interpretation: Straight Lines
theory_units.summary: Straight lines generally suggest masculinity and strength.
theory_units.applies_when: When wishing to evoke feelings of masculinity or strength through compositional lines.
theory_units.expected_effect: Conveys a sense of power and robustness to the viewer.

theory_units.title: Line Interpretation: Softly Curved Lines
theory_units.summary: Softly curved lines suggest femininity and delicate qualities.
theory_units.applies_when: When wishing to evoke feelings of femininity or delicacy through compositional lines.
theory_units.expected_effect: Conveys a sense of grace and tenderness to the viewer.

theory_units.title: Line Interpretation: Sharply Curved Lines
theory_units.summary: Sharply curved lines suggest action and gaiety.
theory_units.applies_when: When wishing to evoke feelings of dynamism, excitement, or cheerfulness through compositional lines.
theory_units.expected_effect: Conveys energy and a playful or active mood.

theory_units.title: Line Interpretation: Long Vertical Curves
theory_units.summary: Long vertical curves with tapering ends suggest dignified beauty and melancholy.
theory_units.applies_when: When wishing to evoke feelings of elegant sadness or solemn grandeur.
theory_units.expected_effect: Conveys a sense of poignant beauty and a contemplative mood.

theory_units.title: Line Interpretation: Long Horizontal Lines
theory_units.summary: Long horizontal lines suggest quiet and restfulness, but paradoxically can also suggest speed.
theory_units.applies_when: When wishing to evoke feelings of calm, repose, or to imply rapid, unhindered movement.
theory_units.expected_effect: Conveys either serenity or a sense of swift progression, depending on context.

theory_units.title: Line Interpretation: Tall Vertical Lines
theory_units.summary: Tall, vertical lines suggest strength and dignity.
theory_units.applies_when: When wishing to evoke feelings of power, integrity, or majesty.
theory_units.expected_effect: Conveys a sense of steadfastness and importance.

theory_units.title: Line Interpretation: Parallel Diagonal Lines
theory_units.summary: Parallel, diagonal lines indicate action, energy, and violence; when converging in the distance, they convey action and energy.
theory_units.applies_when: When wishing to evoke dynamism, conflict, or aggressive force.
theory_units.expected_effect: Conveys a sense of movement, tension, and powerful drive.

theory_units.title: Line Interpretation: Opposing Diagonals
theory_units.summary: Opposing diagonals suggest conflict and forcefulness.
theory_units.applies_when: When wishing to visually represent confrontation, struggle, or strong opposing forces.
theory_units.expected_effect: Creates a sense of tension and dramatic opposition.

theory_units.title: Line Interpretation: Strong, Heavy, Sharp Lines
theory_units.summary: Strong, heavy, sharp lines suggest brightness, laughter, and excitement.
theory_units.applies_when: When wishing to evoke feelings of vivacity, joy, or intense activity.
theory_units.expected_effect: Conveys a vibrant and energetic atmosphere.

theory_units.title: Line Interpretation: Soft Lines
theory_units.summary: Soft lines suggest solemnity and tranquility.
theory_units.applies_when: When wishing to evoke feelings of seriousness, peace, or reverence.
theory_units.expected_effect: Conveys a serene and contemplative atmosphere.

theory_units.title: Line Interpretation: Irregular Lines
theory_units.summary: Irregular lines are generally more interesting than regular lines due to their visual quality.
theory_units.applies_when: When aiming for a composition that is visually engaging and dynamic.
theory_units.expected_effect: Increased visual interest and a less predictable, more organic feel.

theory_units.title: Extending Verticals Beyond Frame
theory_units.summary: Unopposed vertical lines that begin at the bottom or end at the top of the picture appear to extend beyond the frame.
theory_units.applies_when: When an object or line is positioned to imply continuation beyond the visible frame.
theory_units.expected_effect: Creates a sense of scale, suggesting the subject is larger than the frame, or implies unseen elements.
theory_units.caution: Can be monotonous if not managed or accented.

theory_units.title: Weakening by Series of Curves
theory_units.summary: A series of curves may weaken a composition unless they are reinforced by vertical or horizontal accents.
theory_units.applies_when: When composing with multiple curved elements.
theory_units.expected_effect: If not accented, the composition may lack stability and clarity; with accents, it can maintain interest and structure.
theory_units.caution: Reinforce curves to prevent a weak composition.

theory_units.title: Profusion of Curves or Diagonals
theory_units.summary: A profusion of curves or diagonals can result in confusion and should only be used to express shocking excitement or uncontrolled action.
theory_units.applies_when: When the narrative specifically calls for expressing chaos, intense excitement, or uncontrollable energy.
theory_units.expected_effect: Conveys a sense of disorientation, dynamism, or emotional intensity.
theory_units.caution: Avoid overuse, as it can lead to visual clutter and viewer confusion.

theory_units.title: Line Interpretation: Diagonal Lines (Movement/Space)
theory_units.summary: Whenever a vertical or horizontal line becomes a diagonal, it appears to recede from or advance toward the viewer. A diagonal parallel to the picture's surface suggests an action line (moving/falling), while a diagonal receding into the distance suggests a space line.
theory_units.applies_when: When using lines to convey depth, motion, or spatial relationships.
theory_units.expected_effect: Creates a dynamic sense of depth, movement, or expansive space, drawing the eye into the picture.

theory_units.title: Line Interpretation: Receding/Diminishing Curve
theory_units.summary: A receding or diminishing curve suggests distant space, as it carries the eye into the picture.
theory_units.applies_when: When aiming to create a sense of vastness or deep perspective.
theory_units.expected_effect: Draws the viewer's eye into the background, enhancing the perception of depth and distance.

theory_units.title: Line Interpretation: Diagonals as Dynamic
theory_units.summary: Diagonals are dynamic and usually suggest instability because they are fundamentally fallen verticals.
theory_units.applies_when: When seeking to convey energy, tension, or a sense of unease and precariousness.
theory_units.expected_effect: Creates visual tension and a feeling of impending change or dramatic impact.

theory_units.title: Line Interpretation: Speed Qualities
theory_units.summary: Straight, angular, or jagged lines (like lightning) give impressions of speed, forcefulness, or vitality. Softly curved lines slow eye speed, creating a leisurely or deliberate pace. Unbroken lines enable faster viewing than broken or erratic lines.
theory_units.applies_when: When trying to control the viewer's eye speed and convey specific emotional or narrative pacing.
theory_units.expected_effect: Manipulates the audience's perception of speed and energy within the frame, influencing mood and tempo.

theory_units.title: Form Interpretation: Triangular Form
theory_units.summary: A triangular form suggests strength, stability, and solidity. It's a compact, closed form that guides the eye continuously without escape, useful for grouping people and achieving dominance through added height.
theory_units.applies_when: When needing to convey strength, arrange groups dynamically, or make one figure dominate.
theory_units.expected_effect: A visually strong and stable composition that naturally directs attention and implies power.

theory_units.title: Form Interpretation: Reverse Triangle
theory_units.summary: A reverse triangle, with its apex at the bottom, can be used but lacks the inherent stability of a pyramid resting on its base.
theory_units.applies_when: When purposefully aiming for a less stable or more dynamic arrangement, or for specific grouping needs (e.g., child between two adults).
theory_units.expected_effect: A composition that feels less grounded or potentially more precarious, drawing attention through imbalance.
theory_units.caution: It lacks the stability of a traditional triangular form.

theory_units.title: Form Interpretation: Circular/Oval Form
theory_units.summary: A circular or oval form tends to tie in and hold the viewer's attention, causing their gaze to wander within the frame without escape.
theory_units.applies_when: When wishing to contain viewer attention within a specific area or subject, creating a sense of unity and enclosure.
theory_units.expected_effect: The viewer's eye is kept within the defined circular or oval boundary, focusing on the contained elements.
theory_units.caution: Lacks the broad base and stability of a pyramid or triangle.

theory_units.title: Form Interpretation: Cross Form
theory_units.summary: The cross is one of the few compositional forms that may be centered due to its equal radiation, inspiring a sense of unity and force. It is considered awesome and powerful.
theory_units.applies_when: When aiming to convey unity, force, or symbolic power, and a centered composition is desired.
theory_units.expected_effect: A strong, unified, and impactful visual statement, often with spiritual or symbolic connotations.
theory_units.caution: Do not place too close to the side of the frame, or its radiance will be weakened.

theory_units.title: Form Interpretation: Radiating Lines
theory_units.summary: Radiating lines (a variation of the cross) seem to expand and attract, spreading joy and laughter, or suggesting growth and emanation from a hub.
theory_units.applies_when: When wishing to convey a sense of outward expansion, attraction, cheerfulness, or energy radiating from a central point.
theory_units.expected_effect: A dynamic and engaging composition that suggests movement, growth, or joyful energy.
